title: 2023 HMMT February Guts Problem 12
statement: The number 770 is written on a blackboard. Melody repeatedly performs moves, where a move consists of subtracting either 40 or 41 from the number on the board. She performs moves until the number is not positive, and then she stops. Let \(N\) be the number of sequences of moves that Melody could perform. Suppose \(N=a \cdot 2^{b}\) where \(a\) is an odd positive integer and \(b\) is a nonnegative integer. Compute \(100 a+b\).

solutions.text:
Notice that if we use the 41 move nine times or less, we will have to make a total of \(\left\lceil\frac{770}{40}\right\rceil=20\) moves, and if we use it ten times or more, we will have to make a total of \(\left\lfloor\frac{770}{40}\right\rfloor=19\) moves. So, doing casework on the number of 40s we use gives

\[\underbrace{\binom{19}{0}+\binom{19}{1}+\binom{19}{2}+\cdots+\binom{19}{9}}_{19 \text { moves }}+\underbrace{\frac{\binom{20}{10}}{2}+\binom{20}{11}+\binom{20}{11}+\cdots+\binom{20}{20}}_{20 \text { moves }} .\]

Using the row sums of Pascal's triangle we have this sum equal to \(\frac{2^{19}}{2}+\frac{2^{20}}{2}=3 \cdot 2^{18}\). The answer is 318 .
